messages.subject: Encounter Rate Variance
parts:
Hi all:

The dataset I am working with comes from a four year study looking at
changes in bird densities over time on a restoration site and a reference
site. One line transect on the restoration site that was ~1 km in length
was repeatedly surveyed over the study period (once per week during the
non-breeding season and once every other week during the non-breeding
season) and two line transects on the reference site of approximately equal
length were repeatedly surveyed on the same schedule as the reference
site.

When I analyzed my data I pooled all observations with sufficient numbers
of observations and treated them as two samples for each species (pre and
post restoration) regardless of detection method (song, call or visual).
For example, all pre-restoration Marsh Wren observations were analyzed as a
sample and all post restoration Marsh Wren observations were analyzed as a
sample.

When I analyzed the data I got an error message saying: "** Warning: Cannot
estimate encounter rate variance empirically as there is only one sample.
Setting encounter rate variance to zero. **". Is it ok to have my
encounter rate variance be zero and still get an accurate estimate of
density?

Also, I had a committee member question my pooling of observations because
of territoriality of some species. He was concerned that if the site was
surveyed repeatedly on the same transect I might be picking up the same
individual birds each time that had breeding territories that overlapped
the transect. Would these territorial individual songbirds that were
detected multiple times over the study period bias my estimate of density?
If so, is there a way to correct for the bias?

Thanks in advance for input.

-Ben
